input.summary: Vehicle manufacturers are announcing production cuts because they cannot obtain microcontrollers, having released foundry capacity when demand collapsed and finding they cannot get it back. The chips are made on mature nodes running at capacity, lead times exceed six months and new fabrication takes years. The industry orders just in time and holds almost no buffer.
input.title: Carmakers cut production because they cannot get chips

input.summary: An animal disease that is almost always fatal and has no vaccine or treatment has been confirmed in a herd in a country that holds roughly half the world's pigs. It survives for months in feed and frozen meat, most of the national herd is in smallholder operations with limited biosecurity, and live animals are trucked long distances to slaughter. The meat is the dominant protein in the national diet and a component of the official price index.
input.title: Livestock disease with no vaccine confirmed in the country holding half the world's herd

input.summary: A new narrowbody airliner has crashed shortly after take-off for the second time in five months, with a flight profile resembling the first. Regulators outside the manufacturer's home country are grounding the type ahead of the home regulator. A flight-control system able to command nose-down trim from a single sensor is under scrutiny and pilots say it was not in their manuals. The model is the manufacturer's best seller with thousands of unfilled orders.
input.title: Second crash of a new airliner type within months prompts foreign regulators to ground it

input.summary: The main equity index fell about 9 percent and recovered most of it within half an hour, with large-company shares printing at a cent and others at absurd highs. Automated liquidity providers withdrew their quotes as volatility rose and orders routed to venues where the only resting bids were placeholders. There is no fundamental news and no credit event.
input.title: Equity index falls nine percent and recovers within the hour on no news

input.summary: The price of an industrial metal rose by two thirds in one session and then doubled again in hours after sanctions risk to supply collided with an enormous short position held by one producer as a hedge. Much of that position sits in bilateral contracts the exchange cannot see, so the clearing house cannot size the margin call it is about to make. The contract has no daily price limit and the physical market is nowhere near these levels.
input.title: Metal price doubles in hours as a producer's hidden short position is squeezed

input.summary: The producer cartel has declined to cut output in the face of a supply glut, choosing to defend market share, and crude fell immediately below the level at which levered shale producers can service their debt. Output has doubled in four years on high-yield borrowing and reserve-based loans underwritten at far higher prices, wells decline steeply and must be redrilled, and bank borrowing-base redeterminations are due in the spring.
input.title: Producer group refuses to cut output and crude falls below the cost of levered drillers

input.summary: A large relative-value fund has told investors it lost more than 40 percent of its capital in a single month. It holds convergence trades at very high leverage, and a sovereign default has widened every spread it is long at once. Counterparties financed it on light margin because of its reputation, none of them knows the size of the positions the others are funding, and any liquidation would be into the same trades they hold themselves.
input.title: Levered fund loses almost half its capital in a month as its hedges correlate

input.summary: A listed payments company's auditor will not sign the annual accounts because it cannot confirm nearly two billion euros supposedly held in trustee accounts abroad, about a quarter of the balance sheet. The company has faced press allegations of accounting irregularities for years; the national regulator responded by investigating the journalists and short sellers. The cash is said to arise from third-party partners whose revenues no outside party has verified.
input.title: Auditor refuses to sign accounts over cash it cannot confirm exists

input.summary: A leaked balance sheet shows that the trading affiliate of a major crypto exchange holds most of its assets in a token the exchange itself created and can influence the price of, rather than in cash. Customer assets are not segregated, there are no audited accounts and no prudential regulator, and the largest competitor has said it will sell its holding of the token. Customers can withdraw instantly and there is no deposit insurance or lender of last resort.
input.title: Crypto exchange faces a withdrawal run after its affiliate's collateral is revealed

input.summary: The largest property developer by sales has warned it may not meet its obligations after regulators imposed leverage limits that cut off the refinancing its model depends on. A large part of its liabilities are not debt but apartments already paid for by households and not yet built. Construction has stopped on many projects, suppliers are unpaid, retail investors are protesting at its offices, and offshore bondholders sit at the bottom of a structure whose assets are onshore.
input.title: Property developer warns it may miss payments on 300 billion dollars of liabilities

input.summary: A top-ten container line has filed for court receivership after its creditor banks refused further support and its owners declined to inject equity. Freight rates have been below cash cost for years because the industry ordered too many ships. About a hundred vessels are at sea carrying billions of dollars of other people's cargo, and ports, tugs and fuel suppliers will not serve a ship whose owner cannot pay.
input.title: Container line files for receivership with a hundred ships at sea

input.summary: Military exercises with declared closure zones overlapping the ports and shipping lanes of a nearby island have been announced in response to a foreign official's visit. The island fabricates the large majority of the world's most advanced logic chips and there is no substitute capacity anywhere; a blockade lasting weeks would halt most electronics production globally. There is no way to tell a demonstration from the start of a quarantine in advance.
input.title: Live-fire exercises encircle the island that fabricates the world's advanced chips

input.summary: A nuclear-armed state has invaded its neighbour in the largest land war in Europe in generations. The invaded country is a major grain exporter and its Black Sea ports are blockaded; the invader supplies a large share of Europe's gas, oil and fertiliser. Sanctions immobilising roughly half the invader's central-bank reserves were announced within days, which has never been done to an economy this large, putting every commodity contract with its counterparties in question.
input.title: Major state invades its neighbour and its central bank reserves are frozen

input.summary: Voters have decided to leave the trading bloc that takes most of the country's exports, against the outcome markets priced the previous evening. The currency fell about 8 percent overnight, the largest one-day fall in its modern history, and the prime minister resigned. The economy runs a current-account deficit near 5 percent of output and depends on foreign inflows, and open-ended property funds hold illiquid buildings against daily-dealing shares.
input.title: Referendum result upends the country's trade relationship and the currency falls eight percent overnight

input.summary: Tariffs have been announced on tens of billions of dollars of imports from the other largest economy following an investigation into technology transfer, and the partner has promised immediate retaliation aimed at politically sensitive agricultural exports. Supply chains assume the bilateral tariff is near zero and stable, and the schedule is now being set unilaterally rather than through the dispute-settlement system.
input.title: Tariffs announced on the largest trading partner, with retaliation promised

input.summary: The World Health Organization has issued a global alert about a severe atypical pneumonia spreading between countries through air travel, after a doctor infected hotel guests who then flew onward. The pathogen has not been identified, there is no test and no treatment, health workers are heavily represented among the cases, and the reported fatality rate among identified cases is high. The affected economies depend on travel, tourism and exports.
input.title: Global alert issued for a severe new respiratory illness spreading by air travel

input.summary: Health authorities report a new influenza A virus of animal origin spreading between people in two countries, with a genetic combination never seen before and no population immunity. Pandemic influenza is the scenario every national preparedness plan is built around. Early reports from the initial outbreak country suggest an alarming fatality rate among young adults, the virus is already in several countries and a matched vaccine would take about six months.
input.title: Novel influenza strain with no population immunity spreads between countries

input.summary: A haemorrhagic fever outbreak has been notified in a region that has never handled the disease, with cases already spread across several districts and two national borders. Case fatality runs above half, there is no licensed vaccine or treatment, transmission occurs through body fluids and is amplified by burial practices, and the affected countries have a handful of physicians per hundred thousand people.
input.title: Haemorrhagic fever crosses borders in countries with almost no doctors

input.summary: The central bank chair has said that the pace of asset purchases could be reduced in coming meetings if the labour market improves, and long yields have risen sharply. Investors reaching for yield through years of near-zero rates have crowded into emerging-market local debt and long duration, and several deficit economies financed by those flows now face an abrupt reversal. No purchase has actually been reduced and no policy has changed.
input.title: Central bank hints at slowing asset purchases and long yields jump

input.summary: Speculators are attacking a currency board peg while simultaneously shorting the local equity market, so that the automatic rise in interest rates the peg delivers pays them on both legs. The board holds foreign reserves several times the monetary base and the mechanics of the peg are not in doubt; what is being tested is the willingness to accept the interest-rate pain, with property prices already down by half.
input.title: Speculators attack a currency board while shorting its equity market

input.summary: A new government has announced large unfunded tax cuts without an independent fiscal forecast, and thirty-year government bond yields have risen by amounts normally seen over years. Pension funds hedge their liabilities with leveraged bond derivatives while holding illiquid assets elsewhere; the yield rise has triggered collateral calls they can only meet by selling the same bonds, pushing yields higher again. The central bank is due to start selling bonds from its own portfolio within days.
input.title: Unfunded tax cuts send long bond yields up and pension hedges into a collateral spiral
